prompt: Which major Tailwind version does this course teach?
explanation: The setup, theme, and source-detection examples use Tailwind v4.

prompt: Which packages are installed for the v4 CLI workflow?
explanation: Tailwind’s v4 CLI is provided as a separate package alongside tailwindcss.

prompt: Which line imports Tailwind into input.css in this course?
explanation: The v4 stylesheet starts with the Tailwind CSS import.

prompt: What is input.css in the starter?

choices.text: The source stylesheet used by the build

explanation: The input contains imports, source configuration, and custom theme definitions.

prompt: What is output.css in the starter?

choices.text: The generated stylesheet linked by HTML

explanation: The CLI writes the stylesheet that the browser loads.

prompt: What does --watch do in a Tailwind CLI command?

choices.text: Keeps rebuilding as source files change

explanation: Watch mode keeps the build process active during local editing.

prompt: Which setup is intentionally not used in this v4 course?
explanation: Mixing older initialization instructions with the v4 workflow can confuse learners.

prompt: What must HTML do to use the compiled styles?
explanation: The browser needs a stylesheet link pointing to the generated CSS file.

prompt: Is the Play CDN the production build workflow taught here?

choices.text: No, it is for development experiments

explanation: The course teaches a compiled stylesheet for the finished project.

prompt: Where should you edit a theme value so rebuilding preserves the change?
explanation: Generated output is replaced by the next build, so change the source.

prompt: What does a Tailwind utility class primarily express?
explanation: Utilities map to CSS declarations and should be understood through their underlying properties.

prompt: Which utility adds padding on all sides?
explanation: The p prefix sets padding rather than margin or layout gutters.

prompt: Which utility adds top margin?
explanation: mt sets margin-top; pt would set padding-top.

prompt: Which utility adds gutters between grid items?
explanation: Gap acts on the layout container to separate items or tracks.

prompt: With the default spacing theme, what is p-4 based on?
explanation: Numeric spacing utilities use the theme’s spacing value, which can be customized.

prompt: What does px-4 control?
explanation: The px utility adds padding on the inline axis.

prompt: What is Preflight’s role?

choices.text: It provides base styles and resets some browser defaults

explanation: Preflight standardizes starting styles, so headings and other elements may need explicit presentation.

prompt: Will the last conflicting class in the HTML attribute always win?

choices.text: No, the generated CSS and cascade decide
Only if the class is shorter

explanation: Class-attribute order is not the ordering of competing CSS declarations.

prompt: Which is a better way to understand a copied card’s classes?

choices.text: Keep every class without reading it
Identify the CSS purpose of each class

explanation: Mapping utilities back to properties makes the design maintainable.

prompt: Does rounded-xl make an element a semantic card or article?

choices.text: Yes, it changes the tag name

explanation: Visual utilities do not supply semantic HTML structure.

prompt: What does text-xl primarily change?
explanation: Tailwind’s named text-size utility controls the type size and its default line height.

prompt: What does text-slate-800 change?
explanation: The color token following text- selects a foreground color.

prompt: Which utility controls font weight?
explanation: The font weight utility changes the weight of the glyphs.

prompt: Which utility controls line height?
explanation: Leading utilities set line height for text.

prompt: Which utility constrains a paragraph to a reading measure?
explanation: A prose-width limit helps prevent excessively wide text lines.

prompt: Why may an h2 need explicit text-size classes with Tailwind?

choices.text: Tailwind turns it into an image

explanation: The semantic heading remains but its visual hierarchy is intentionally styled.

prompt: What should accompany border-slate-300 to make a normal card border visible?

choices.text: A border-width utility such as border

explanation: Color alone does not supply a visible border width.

prompt: Does using a named palette color guarantee sufficient contrast?

choices.text: No, check the actual foreground/background pair

explanation: Accessibility depends on the colors in combination and the text or control context.

prompt: Which element best preserves a card heading’s meaning?

choices.text: A decorative image of the text

explanation: Utilities can style a proper heading without replacing its semantics.

prompt: Which review is appropriate after changing a surface color?

choices.text: Recheck text, border, and focus contrast

explanation: A changed surface alters several important visual relationships.

prompt: Which class makes a container’s direct children flex items?
explanation: The flex display utility establishes the flex layout context.

prompt: Which combination creates a two-column grid?
explanation: The container needs grid display and a column-template utility.

prompt: Which utility allows a flex toolbar to wrap?
explanation: Flex wrapping lets items flow to another line when space is limited.

prompt: In a row-direction flex toolbar, what does items-center align?
explanation: Items utilities correspond to align-items and use the cross axis in Flexbox.

prompt: What does justify-between do in a flex container?

choices.text: Distributes main-axis free space between items

explanation: The utility maps to space-between distribution along the main axis.

prompt: What can min-w-0 help a flex or grid item do?

choices.text: Shrink below its automatic minimum width

explanation: A zero minimum can allow shrinking around long content, which may also need wrapping.

prompt: Which class provides container gutters?
explanation: Gap separates items or tracks in supported layouts.

prompt: What does grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 describe?

choices.text: One base column and two from md upward

explanation: The unprefixed rule is the base and the responsive variant enhances wider layouts.

prompt: Should order utilities be used without reviewing keyboard and reading order?

choices.text: Yes, they always update all reading order
Yes, if the cards are colorful
No, source and visual order can disagree

explanation: Layout reordering should not create a confusing interaction sequence.

prompt: Where should the grid display utility be applied for a set of task cards?
explanation: The layout model is established by the container around its direct children.

prompt: What does an unprefixed Tailwind utility represent in responsive styling?

choices.text: A base rule that can apply at every width

explanation: Unprefixed utilities establish the base until another matching rule changes the same property.

prompt: Does sm: mean “only small phones”?

choices.text: No, it applies from the sm minimum width upward
It applies only to a named phone

explanation: Default responsive variants use minimum widths rather than exclusive device categories.

prompt: With the default theme, where does md begin?
explanation: The default md breakpoint is 48rem, though themes can customize it.

prompt: What does p-4 md:p-8 do?

choices.text: Uses smaller base padding and larger padding from md upward

explanation: The responsive variant replaces the padding value when its condition matches.

prompt: Why is the viewport meta tag still needed in a Tailwind page?

choices.text: Mobile layout still depends on correct viewport behavior

explanation: Using utility classes does not remove the normal HTML viewport requirement.

prompt: Which class is a complete responsive utility?
explanation: A full class name can be detected and compiled by Tailwind.

prompt: How should the smallest-screen font size be expressed?
explanation: The base style covers widths below the first breakpoint as well as larger widths unless overridden.

prompt: What should decide whether a two-column breakpoint works?

choices.text: The content remains readable and controls remain usable

explanation: Responsive choices need to work for actual content and interaction.

prompt: Can Tailwind breakpoints be customized?
explanation: The default breakpoint values are theme decisions rather than universal constants.

prompt: Which test can reveal problems missed by a clean demo?

choices.text: Long text plus narrow width and zoom

explanation: Realistic content and enlarged views exercise wrapping, sizing, and access.

prompt: Which variant styles an element during pointer hover?
explanation: The hover variant applies when the corresponding pointer state matches.

prompt: Which variant helps create a visible keyboard focus indicator?
explanation: Focus-visible styles provide feedback when focus should be visibly indicated.

prompt: Does disabled:opacity-50 itself disable a button?

choices.text: No, the button must actually be disabled

explanation: The variant styles an existing native state and does not create the disabled behavior.

prompt: Which attribute provides a native disabled button state?
explanation: The disabled attribute changes the native control’s behavior as well as its state.

prompt: Which class marks a parent for group-based state variants?
explanation: Group variants respond to the state of a parent marked with group.

prompt: What is a peer variant commonly based on?

choices.text: The state of a preceding sibling marked peer

explanation: Peer variants use sibling relationships and require the appropriate marked sibling.

prompt: Which utility variant can remove a transition for reduced-motion users?
explanation: The motion-reduce condition respects the user’s reduced-motion preference.

prompt: What does focus-visible:outline-offset-2 adjust?

choices.text: Spacing between the focused element and its outline

explanation: Outline offset can separate the focus indicator from the element edge.

prompt: Do Tailwind state classes implement task saving?

choices.text: No, behavior must be implemented separately

explanation: Tailwind handles styling, not storage, application events, or server logic.

prompt: What should you check besides hover on a styled link?

choices.text: Only whether it has a shadow

explanation: Links need clear feedback for keyboard interaction as well as pointer use.

prompt: Which v4 directive declares variables that participate in Tailwind’s theme?
explanation: The theme directive registers design variables used by utility generation.

prompt: Which theme variable can support a bg-brand utility?
explanation: The color namespace connects a token to color utilities.

prompt: What is the purpose of bg-brand?

choices.text: Use the registered brand background color

explanation: A generated color utility applies the theme value to a CSS property.

prompt: Does declaring --color-brand only in :root automatically register new Tailwind utilities?

choices.text: Only if the value is red
Yes, every custom property becomes a class
No, use the Tailwind theme mechanism

explanation: Ordinary custom properties and Tailwind theme variables have different roles.

prompt: When can a custom theme utility be generated by source detection?

choices.text: Only if a user clicks it
Only if it appears in a screenshot
When its complete class name is present in a scanned source

explanation: The compiler needs a complete detected utility candidate and its supporting theme definition.

prompt: What is a good reason to use a named theme color?

choices.text: Express a shared design role consistently

explanation: Named tokens communicate and centralize a design decision.

prompt: When is an arbitrary value most appropriate?

choices.text: For a deliberate exception that the theme does not cover
For every repeated spacing value by default

explanation: A small system benefits from shared values with intentional exceptions.

prompt: What should you do after changing a shared theme color?

choices.text: Recheck all affected color pairs and focus states
Assume every component is still readable

explanation: A shared token affects multiple components and interaction states.

prompt: Where does this course place its v4 theme definitions?
explanation: The input stylesheet is the source for imports and theme configuration.

prompt: Why keep the theme small at first?

choices.text: It makes design decisions easier to use and maintain

explanation: A focused set of intentional values is easier to apply consistently.

prompt: What does Tailwind’s default dark: variant follow?
explanation: The default variant uses the system color-scheme preference.

prompt: Which class provides a dark-mode card background?
explanation: The dark variant conditionally applies the chosen background utility.

prompt: Why is changing only the dark background risky?

choices.text: Existing text and borders may become unreadable

explanation: Readable dark mode requires coordinated foreground, surface, border, and state colors.

prompt: Does a moon icon by itself implement a working theme toggle?
explanation: A custom toggle requires actual state-changing behavior and a configured strategy.

prompt: What extra setup is needed for a manual selector-based dark strategy?

choices.text: A matching custom variant plus behavior to set the selector

explanation: The selector condition and the control that changes it must agree.

prompt: Why does the phase-two starter show no custom dark-mode toggle?
explanation: The starter uses a working default rather than displaying an inert control.

prompt: Which utility pairs with text-slate-900 for lighter dark-mode text?
explanation: The foreground needs a suitable value on the dark surface.

prompt: Does dark mode replace contrast review?

choices.text: Yes, every dark palette is accessible

explanation: Color relationships need to remain readable in each mode.

prompt: What is a useful dark-mode testing procedure?

choices.text: Switch the system appearance and inspect every surface and control

explanation: The default variant can be tested by changing the preference it follows.

prompt: Should a dark-mode change alter the page’s semantic heading structure?

choices.text: No, preserve the same meaningful structure

explanation: Color-scheme styling should not remove semantic content or navigation structure.

prompt: How does Tailwind discover classes in source files?

choices.text: By scanning source text for complete class names

explanation: Source detection recognizes full utility candidates without running application code.

prompt: Why can a constructed string such as bg- plus a color variable fail?

choices.text: Every variable is forbidden in HTML
The complete utility may never appear in scanned text

explanation: The compiler cannot infer arbitrary runtime string assembly.

prompt: Which approach makes conditional color classes detectable?

choices.text: Map choices to complete class strings

explanation: Full class names in scanned source can be recognized and generated.

prompt: What does @source register in Tailwind v4?
explanation: The source directive identifies files that should participate in class detection.

prompt: In the taught @source example, paths are relative to what?
explanation: Source paths in the directive are resolved relative to the stylesheet.

prompt: What is the purpose of source(none) in the starter’s Tailwind import?

choices.text: Disable automatic source detection so explicit sources control scanning

explanation: The starter explicitly lists its HTML source instead of scanning unrelated folders.

prompt: Which CLI option compacts the generated stylesheet?
explanation: Minification reduces the generated output representation for delivery.

prompt: How should a one-time release build behave?
explanation: A final build produces the artifact without requiring an ongoing watcher.

prompt: Why avoid hand-editing output.css as the main workflow?

choices.text: The next build replaces generated output
It has no effect in browsers

explanation: Maintain changes in source files so builds reproduce them.

prompt: What should be moved together when checking the finished static package?

choices.text: HTML and its referenced generated CSS

explanation: Relative stylesheet links require the output file to be available with the intended folder structure.

prompt: What is the central project in the Tailwind course?

choices.text: Rebuild the student planner with utilities

explanation: Reusing the planner lets learners compare styling workflows on the same content.

prompt: What should remain consistent between the plain CSS and Tailwind versions?
explanation: Different styling approaches should preserve the meaning and usability of the page.

prompt: What does npm run build do in the supplied Tailwind starter?
explanation: The starter’s build script runs the Tailwind CLI once to generate CSS.

prompt: What is npm run dev used for in the starter?
explanation: The development script uses watch mode for local source changes.

prompt: Why does the starter include compiled CSS as well as sources?

choices.text: It can be opened immediately and rebuilt when edited

explanation: A ready output makes the starter inspectable while sources preserve the learning workflow.

prompt: Which README comparison demonstrates understanding?

choices.text: Only which version has more classes
Tradeoffs in readability, reuse, builds, and maintenance

explanation: The same project makes it possible to explain meaningful differences between approaches.

prompt: Does this phase’s polished task form persist tasks?

choices.text: No, it remains a clearly labelled static prototype

explanation: Styling and compilation do not implement application storage.

prompt: What should a completed project review include?

choices.text: Keyboard, narrow width, zoom, and both color schemes

explanation: The project should be checked in realistic interaction and viewing conditions.

prompt: How should you handle a copied utility that you cannot explain?

choices.text: Look up its CSS effect and test whether it is needed

explanation: Understanding each utility makes future changes more reliable.

prompt: What does marking the project complete represent in this course?

choices.text: Automatic certification of a deployed app
A guarantee that every video was watched

explanation: The project is self-assessed and separate from quiz scoring or deployment.
